comparison: Both address biosensor development and validation (C3-C6, C23-C34). OpenEval finds the design well-documented and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to missing optimization procedures, incomplete construct details, and lack of bleed-through characterization, indicating insufficient documentation of core methodology.

OpenEval R5 addresses biosensor validation (C30-C34) which overlaps with peer R1. OpenEval finds validation SUPPORTED through titration and controls. Peer reviewers include these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation due to missing technical details about optimization and characterization.

Both evaluate compound 3344 as RAS-effector PPI inhibitor (C39-C40). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED by NMR binding and BRET data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising critical concern that Kd determination uses concentrations far above estimated Kd and requesting alternative biophysical validation.

OpenEval R7 addresses 3344 specificity (C41-C43), while peer R3 addresses broader inhibition claims (C41-C43, C49-C53). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation times (20h) that may allow indirect effects through autocrine pathways rather than direct PPI inhibition.

Both address pan-mutant KRAS inhibition (C49-C53). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by dose-response BRET and western blots. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation times that prevent ruling out indirect signaling effects, requesting short-term assays.

Both address iDAb RAS validation (C35-C38). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as strong validation of biosensor. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, treating iDAb experiments as adequate positive controls without specific concerns.

OpenEval R8 addresses full-length CRAF biosensor coupling to signaling (C44-C48). Peer R9 addresses subset (C46-C48). Both find SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers raising no specific concerns about iDAb validation experiments.

OpenEval R8 addresses CRAFFL biosensor development (C44-C48), peer R10 addresses subset (C44-C45). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers treat this methodological improvement as adequately documented without specific concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C54-C58) on wild-type KRAS under EGF stimulation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by EGF-induced BRET and dose-dependent inhibition. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation times (3hr and 20hr) that may allow indirect autocrine effects.

Both address PI3K pathway biosensor (C59-C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by p85α requirement, specificity controls, and pAKT reduction. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation concerns and lack of optimization/construct documentation for this complex tripartite system.

Both address 3344 inhibition of RAS-PI3K pathway (C63-C68). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by dose-response BRET and pAKT reduction. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation times and insufficient technical documentation.

High overlap on RAS family member breadth (C70-C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by comprehensive BRET data across NRAS and HRAS. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting high quality data with no specific concerns about these family members.

Both address structural validation (C75-C76, C83-C85). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by crystal structure and modeling showing overlap with effector sites. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting replacement of Figure 6B with illustration of effector interference and clarification about switch region conformational changes.

Both address 3344 effects in cancer cells with endogenous RAS (C77-C79, C88). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by western blots showing dose-dependent signaling reduction. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation times preventing confirmation that effects are direct rather than indirect.

Both address IC50 differences between overexpression and endogenous systems (C88-C89). OpenEval finds observation SUPPORTED but explanation speculative. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, treating the explanation as reasonable speculation without challenge.

OpenEval R18 addresses IC50 observation (C88), which peer R8 includes. OpenEval notes observation is SUPPORTED but explanation uncertain. Peer R8 rates broader claims UNCERTAIN due to incubation time concerns about mechanism.

Both address biosensor utility and capabilities (C80-C82, C86-C87, C93). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by comprehensive validation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting interest to community but stating utility claims not fully supported until essential revisions address optimization, documentation, and technical validation issues.

High overlap on future applications (C91-C92, C94-C96). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as speculative about future uses rather than demonstrated capabilities. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, appropriately treating these as speculative possibilities rather than demonstrated results.
Both address background on RAS clinical significance (C1-C2, C8-C11). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established literature. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, not questioning these contextual claims.
Both address RAS biology background (C12-C19). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established scientific knowledge. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED as established background facts with citations.

Both address rationale for cell-based assays (C20-C22). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by citations and standard drug development principles. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, not questioning these contextual claims.

Perfect claim overlap (C97-C100) on methodological details and data availability. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are straightforward factual claims. Peer reviewers note these are factual statements, requesting additional information but not challenging the specific claims made.

OpenEval R16 addresses overarching conclusion about pan-inhibitor characterization (C7, C58, C74). Finds SUPPORTED by comprehensive evidence across all experiments. No corresponding peer evaluation specifically addresses this synthesis claim.
